THIS DEVICE IS NO LONGER IN PRODUCTION Palisades® Mega Ultimate Overdrive The Palisades is something we said we would never do… an overdrive based on the legendary TS808! After loads of requests, we finally buckled. We ran tests with every popular clone on the market as well as several vintage originals, compared, contrasted and took loads of notes. It was exhausting but informative. In the end, we threw it all away, used our ears and came up with what we feel is the most versatile relative of the 808 available today. With 6 different clipping voices, 5 bandwidth settings and 2 gain channels, you will be hard-pressed to not find a setting that will wipe every mid-boosting overdrive off your board. The Palisades is a versatile dude that will give you years of loving companionship. View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize Controls     1. Boost: Sets the level of the output boost. 2. Gain A: Sets the gain for the Channel A (lower gain) 3. Volume: Sets the output level. 4. Gain B: Sets the gain for Channel B (higher gain) 5. Tone: Brighter clockwise, warmer counterclockwise. Rotary Switches 6. Voice: This sets the nature of the Palisades distortion by changing the clipping diodes. No diodes: The most open and least distorted. LED clipping: Light clipping with a lot of volume. Mosfet clipping: Light gain OD with great harmonics. Asymmetrical Silicon clipping: Tighter light gain OD closest to stock 808. Symmetrical silicon clipping: Tighter distorted tone. Schottky Diode clipping: Looser fuzzy tone. 7. Bandwidth: This sets the overall tone and gain structure of the Palisades. 1 is the thinnest setting with the least amount of gain and 5 is the fattest setting with the heaviest gain. Everything else is in between. This control has a major effect on all the settings of the Palisades, especially the Gain and Voice controls. Toggle Switches 8. Normal/Bright: Normal is a warm full tone. Bright is livelier tone with more chime. 9. Buffer: Turns the input buffer on or off. ON is a tighter and brighter tone while OFF is a warmer tone with more sag. The buffer is part of the drive circuit & is only available when the Palisades is activated. Foot Switches 10. Boost: Activates the output level boost, Features Flexi-Switching. 11. Gain B: Activates Gain Channel B, Features Flexi-Switching. 12. Activate: True bypass switch Audio Samples GUITAR SAMPLES Gain A & B Gibson Les Paul Gain A & B No Diode Gibson Les Paul Gain A & B then Boost Gibson Les Paul Gain A & B then Boost (Both Fuzz & Shift Sweeps) Gibson Les Paul Pete's Paul Gibson Les Paul Still Love You Gibson Les Paul View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize Tech Specs Dimensions: 4.75 x 5.65 x 2.25 in. History, V1 vs V2, verified players, tone recipes and buying advice. admin 22 September 2026 21 min read GG-ARTICLE-TOP Every boutique pedal company eventually builds a Tube Screamer. It is a rite of passage, like a bar band learning “Mustang Sally.” EarthQuaker Devices spent years insisting they were the exception — that the Akron workshop turning out fuzzes named after geological formations and doom-metal album titles had no interest in reheating the most cloned circuit in the history of the guitar. GG-ARTICLE-AFTER-INTRO Then, in May 2014, they gave in. And because it is EarthQuaker, they did not give in quietly. The Palisades arrived with five knobs, two rotary switches, two toggles, three footswitches and a subtitle — Mega Ultimate Overdrive — that reads less like a product name than a dare. Six clipping voices. Five bandwidth settings. Two independent gain channels. A separate boost. An input buffer you can switch out of the circuit entirely. Thirty distinct versions of the effect before you touch a single knob. EarthQuaker’s own launch copy did not pretend otherwise: “The Palisades is something we said we would never do… an overdrive based on the legendary TS808! After loads of requests, we finally buckled.” This is a feature, not a review. We are not handing out stars. We are here to explain what the Palisades actually is, what those thirty combinations really do, which players genuinely used one — and why a pedal this ambitious is now sitting on the discontinued list, hunted on the used market by people who should have bought one in 2019. How to Get the Tone ↓ Akron’s Anti-Tube-Screamer, And Why It Took Them Six Years EarthQuaker Devices’ origin story — Jamie Stillman, a basement in Akron, Ohio, a company built by a touring musician who got tired of touring — is told in full in our features on the EarthQuaker Devices Hoof Fuzz and the Acapulco Gold , so we will not repeat it here. What matters for the Palisades is the house philosophy that story produced: EarthQuaker built its reputation on pedals nobody else was making. Bit crushers. Octave-up monsters. Reverbs with a control literally labelled “Drag.” A one-knob distortion with no tone control at all. A Tube Screamer clone is the exact opposite of that.
